lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.13 - A Listen, point, and say

details: Listen, point and say checks understanding of word meaning and sound. Listen and point shows students can  match what they hear to the right image. Say practises first-step pronunciation.
Look for careful listening, correct pointing, clear sounds and confident repetition.
“It’s my first day of school. I  need to pack my bag but I don’t know what to put in it. Can you help me find things to put in my bag?”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together: 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.13 - B Listen and circle

details: Listen and circle gives students controlled practice identifying the target language and exposes them to the structure What’s this…? It’s a….
Look for accurate and confident identification and circling of the correct school item.
“Ok, I’m at school now and I think I’ve got everything I need. There’s just one thing I can’t find. Can you help me?”

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p.64 - A Look & number

details: Look and number strengthens recognition of target words. Students look at the pictures and locate the words that match them, reinforcing whole-word memory.
Look for correct identification of all six words, and accurate numbering of the boxes.
“Uh oh, without the words next to the pictures I keep forgetting the names for everything I need.  Please read the words for me, then help put the correct numbers in the boxes.”

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p.64 - B Look and write

details: Look and write gives students controlled practice spelling the target words and identifying individual letters within the words. It reinforces letter order and neat handwriting.
Look for correct spelling, consistent letter formation, and neat handwriting within the lines.

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.14 - C. Ask and answer

details: Ask and answer gives students controlled practice of using ‘this’ to talk about objects that are near to them.
Look for correct use of ‘What’s this…?’, clear answers beginning with ‘It’s a…’ and consistent reference to the objects in the picture.
“I’m not sure I like school. It’s so hard to remember everything. How do I ask what something is if I don’t know its name? Can you help me?”

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.14 - D. Roll a die. Then ask and answer.

details: Roll a die provides the opportunity to further use the target structure in a more engaging way.
Look for accurate use of the target language, correct pronunciation, and natural turn-taking with classmates.
“You have been so helpful - I now know how to ask the names of things. Can you help me practice a bit more?”

The chant strengthens retention of the target language and helps improve pronunciation and stress.
Look for correct stress, confident participation, with most students able to join in with at least the most repeated parts of the chant.
“I learnt so much on my first day! Now I just have to remember to bring everything again tomorrow. Say this chant with me to help me remember!”
